text:
Florida arrives in Columbus on a short fuse. The Panthers lost 4-1 at Boston on Sunday, a game where Jeremy Swayman made 40 saves, and they're 2-3-0 in their last five while playing without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, both on injured reserve. Columbus is also 2-3-0 over its last five and comes off a 5-2 loss at Buffalo, with three days of rest. Florida won the first meeting 7-3 on Oct 13, though by our numbers the Panthers deserved that one only 49% of the time.

Our numbers see little separating them. At five on five, Florida has taken 52% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and Columbus 49%. The Panthers take almost six penalties a game, which keeps feeding opponents power plays. In net, projected starter Jacob Markstrom sits at -0.8 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals he's saved compared with an average goalie facing the same shots), while Columbus's projected Cam Talbot is at +5.6 after a .940 stretch over his last five starts. Last season, both were below zero.

With Marchand out, Matthew Tkachuk has moved onto Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk's line. He has a four-game point streak and is 74% for a point tonight. Zach Werenski has a six-game point streak and sits at 70%. Our under-the-radar pick is Columbus's Adam Fantilli, 52% for a point, above what his season pace says, because his line creates chances at 3.88 expected goals per 60 with him on the ice.
